Chapter 2: Expanding the Luck Surface Area—Visibility, Value, and Connection.
So, if luck isn’t just something that happens to us, what can we actually do to make it more likely? Let’s dig into this idea of the “luck surface area.” Think of it like casting a bigger net in the ocean—the wider you spread it, the more fish, or in this case, lucky breaks, you’re likely to catch.
Your luck surface area really comes down to two things: the value you create, and how visible that value is to others. Creating value is all about doing meaningful work—maybe you’re solving tough problems, sharing what you’ve learned, or building something that helps people. But if nobody ever sees this work, your chances for serendipity are pretty limited, right?
Let’s picture a brilliant engineer who quietly comes up with groundbreaking solutions but keeps them tucked away within a small team. Their impact—and their luck—stays small. Now, compare that to someone who not only invents, but also gets out there, shares their story, connects, and collaborates. Every blog post, every conversation, every conference is another spot where luck could strike.
So, how do you actually expand your own luck surface area? Here are a few habits that make a real difference:
First, share your progress and lessons learned openly. Don’t just talk about the polished end results. Let people in on the messy process, the setbacks, and what you’re figuring out along the way. This not only helps others, but it invites feedback and attracts collaborators who might just open doors you never expected.
Next, dive into communities and networks. Whether it’s an industry meetup, an online group, or just grabbing coffee with new people, every interaction is a chance to cross paths with fresh ideas—and maybe, the right person at the right time.
And don’t forget to offer help and seek input. When you’re generous with your time and genuinely curious about others, you build relationships that often lead to surprising introductions and insights down the road.
Here’s a real-world example: think about a designer who starts posting sketches and thoughts on social media. At first, it’s just for fun. But over time, those posts catch the eye of a startup founder searching for creative talent. What began as a simple habit of sharing ends up turning into a life-changing career opportunity.
Now, increasing your visibility doesn’t mean you have to become a shameless self-promoter. It’s more about being authentic and open—sharing not only your wins, but also the struggles and unfinished ideas. When you do this, you signal to others that you’re approachable and real, which makes people want to connect, collaborate, or even help out.
What’s really powerful is how value creation and visibility feed off each other. The more value you create, the more you have to share. The more visible you become, the more feedback and opportunities come your way. It’s a cycle that turns luck from just wishful thinking into something you can actually practice and build.
So, the heart of expanding your luck surface area is about making yourself discoverable—and indispensable. It’s about committing to meaningful work, and making sure the right people see it. By focusing on both value and visibility, you lay down the foundation for serendipity to play a bigger, more active role in your career and your life.
